Lamborghini Temerario Spyder Delivers Open-Air Access to Its 10,000-RPM V-8

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned.
  • Sources indicate that formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning.
  • Industry observers note that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned. Of course, there was a convertible version of the Temerario coming. And on Wednesday, November 18, the automaker unveiled it for the first time—and it is called, of course, the Temerario Spyder.

Sources indicate that formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning. The Temerario was designed with the Spyder always in mind; as such, there’s space enough behind the two seats for the latest power folding hardtop to snick down inside almost perfectly vertically. The firewall between the cockpit and the mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged V-8 doesn’t change its location, but the space behind the seats is utilized differently.

Industry observers note that the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California. This is the first Lambo to use a retractable hardtop.

In a recent development, 10 electric actuators split the two-piece top, open a hatch behind the seats, and move the structure down into its narrow warren. It’s a fully electric system, so there are no hydraulic lines to split open. Lamborghini says the power top adds about 100 kilograms (220 pounds) to the Temerario’s mass, but that’s all at the center of the car, so that front-to-rear weight balance is maintained. With the roof open, says the maker, the center of gravity drops about three millimeters from where it is when closed.

Recent findings suggest that the hardtop should also produce close to a coupe-like experience when it is closed.“We reinforce the structure of the Spyder,” explains Fermin Soneira, Lambo’s chief technical officer, about the Temerario Spyder’s aluminum space frame. “So, for example, we use some hydroformed pieces in place of castings at some points.”.

The Temerario Spyder takes the market position that was once held by the Huracan Spyder, and Lamborghini claims this upcoming architecture is six percent stiffer in torsional rigidity and nine percent up in dynamic bending stiffness than that car. If all that stiff isn’t stiffy enough, there’s also a six percent increase in dynamic torsional rigidity. So, it’s a super-stiffy thing.

The increase in weight means the suspension has been slightly tweaked to deal with it. “If you change the weight, you have to change the spring rate to keep the same natural frequency,” indicates Soneira. “In this case, it was not about leaving everything the same, but also about increasing comfort in the ‘Strada’ drive mode. Still, if you go to the Hockenheimring, there’s less than a one second per lap difference between the coupe and the Spyder.”.

Recent findings suggest that top up or down, the most spectacular element of every Temerario is the flat-plane crank, 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 that’s incorporated into the hybrid all-wheel drive powertrain. With a lightweight reciprocating assembly that includes titanium connecting rods, the engine will spin to a thrilling 10,000-rpm redline. “We have a latest calibration of the engine sound,” adds Soneira, “so you end up with a slightly different voice than in the coupe. The target is always ‘let’s keep improving,’ so these changes will come to the coupe too.”.

According to recent reports, combined with three electric motors, the Temerario has 907 horsepower aboard—and despite all the electronic hickey-doos, it still stirs up and blasts like a true supercar. That’s not likely to change with the Spyder.

Production of the Spyder will be done in batches along the regular Temerario assembly line, with the first saleable models due to be completed as this is published. Lamborghini expects about 50 percent of Temerario production to be Spyders. Prices haven’t been announced, but should start around $400,000 and go up from there only limited by the buyer’s imagination and wallet.

A graduate of UC Santa Barbara, he still lives near that campus with his wife and two children. He owns a pair of Toyota Tundras and two dogs. He used to have a Nova and a Camaro.

Holiday Gift Guide 2026

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2575 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that with the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day.
  • We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap.
  • Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this newly introduced expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen shows the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399.

Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this newly introduced expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50.

Sources indicate that if you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250.

For players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The latest Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99.

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! New entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46.

It has been revealed that we’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some consumers with the original – it wasn’t big enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119.

In a recent development, privacy around smart glasses has been a major point of contention as wearable tech continues to expand. Even G2s have a clear answer to that issue by consciously leaving out a camera. Instead, these glasses focus on productivity and specific tasks, like real-time translation into 35 languages, in-lens teleprompters for presentations, and calendar notifications – all presented in a readable display that is largely invisible from the outside. $600.

In a recent development, if you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99.

It has been revealed that the question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900.

According to recent reports, if the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250.

It’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50.

It has been revealed that while the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230.

Across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650.

Recent findings suggest that the original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25.

In a recent development, many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21.

If you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s notable that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a significant selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300.

According to recent reports, beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned promptly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65.

Console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199.

This tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99.

The original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169.

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299.

Industry observers note that role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50.

In a recent development, as gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300.

With an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299.

SteelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The new Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260.

Valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the company has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but presently the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059.

Many of the coolest “gaming lights” focus on the flexibility and fun of bright RGB customization. While we’re fans of that aesthetic, it leaves others out in the cold who might want something a bit more natural. The Elements hex panels feature a natural wood-inspired panel, customizable “scenes” like a campfire glow, and can react to both music and touch, with adjustable ambient white light to keep the vibe relaxed. $200.

Kyle Hilliard contributed to this article.

Latest Update: Machina Aims to Democratize Car Customization with Innovative Robots

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (948 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, automotive manufacturing is a laborious, resource-intensive process.
  • Industry observers note that machina’s business is based around its RoboCraftsman platform, which it basically pitches as a factory in a box.
  • Recent findings suggest that machina Labs was founded in 2019 and so far has mostly served clients in the aerospace and defense industries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, automotive manufacturing is a laborious, resource-intensive process. While the complex metropolises that are modern car factories work well for high-volume products, it is often prohibitively expensive for automakers to retool these plants to create distinct body panels for limited-production models. Now a California-based organization called Machina Labs aims to plug that gap with an innovative metal manufacturing process that promises speed, flexibility, and cost-savings.

See all results for used cars for sale near 11566.

Industry observers note that machina’s business is based around its RoboCraftsman platform, which it basically pitches as a factory in a box. The system uses a pair of large robotic arms to perform a variety of tasks on metal panels, from striking designs into pre-stamped panels to fully forming fresh pieces. The robotic arms are controlled by software that can switch between different projects as rapidly as Machina can upload new designs, and the system also scans the completed panel to see if any additional work needs to be done, and to trim, finish, and heat treat the pieces. The entire setup can be folded into two shipping containers that can then be easily transported.

Recent findings suggest that machina Labs was founded in 2019 and so far has mostly served clients in the aerospace and defense industries. But now Machina wants to enter the automotive space, launching a fresh division called Machina Rebellis. With its RoboCraftsman platform, Machina aims to give automakers a way to skip the costly retooling process, with its technology providing a more efficient method to swiftly craft customizable body panels, allowing OEMs to efficiently build more distinctive limited-edition cars.

Industry observers note that machina’s interest in the automotive world started a few years back when it built a truck called the Anvil, based on the Ford F-150 Lightning, to demonstrate the unique body panels its metalworking machines could produce. While still fairly crude, this early prototype got Toyota’s attention, and the Japanese automotive giant is now an investor in Machina Labs via Woven Capital, Toyota’s venture capital division.

The process has improved vastly since the Anvil was built, and to demonstrate this, Machina Labs created a upcoming show vehicle, the Lassen, which is being shown at the Los Angeles auto show. Based on a Toyota Tacoma, the Lassen wears a unique hood, tailgate, and fenders, showing off the sort of customization that Machina’s process is capable of. Machina worked with Callum, the design house formed by Ian Callum, to pen the look of these panels before manufacturing them using the RoboCraftsman platform.

See all results for used cars for sale near 11566.

In a recent development, while the Lassen isn’t a drastic departure from a standard Tacoma, the changes that Machina made would typically take around four to six months to produce via traditional methods, the company said at a media event at its second factory in Chatsworth, California. Using its RoboCraftsman platform, Machina was able to take the Lassen from sketches to a finished product in just two and a half weeks.

The Lassen demonstrates off Machina’s two main capabilities. The hood and tailgate demonstrate the RoboCraftsman’s ability to re-strike pre-stamped panels with custom designs. The Lassen’s tailgate has a bold embossed Machina script, while the hood also states Machina and has a topographical map of its namesake, Mount Lassen in California. The RoboCraftsman platform can put just about any design on a metal panel, and Machina also had tailgates on display featuring a retro Toyota design and a Los Angeles Rams logo.

The fenders, meanwhile, are entirely fresh panels formed by the RoboCraftsman, and they have a bulging, powerful look. These fenders started as a sheet of metal—Machina works in both aluminum and steel—before being shaped by the robotic arms. This process is a bit slower than the re-striking process, which can take minutes to complete, but a fully formed panel can be finished within hours.

Machina believes its RoboCraftsman platform is best suited to production runs in the hundreds and thousands. This could include special-edition models for large OEMs, or working with aftermarket companies to create body kits and other visual customizations. OEMs can also use Machina’s process to promptly create body panels for early pre-production vehicles, typically an expensive and time-consuming part of the development cycle. In the future, Machina also envisions sending its RoboCraftsman units directly to OEM manufacturing sites to speed up the process even further.

Sources indicate that over the past decade, high-end carmakers realized there is a lot of money in personalization, leading to a surge of one-off and limited-production supercars, designed to the exacting specification desired by their wealthy buyers. These cars, often hand-built, are incredibly expensive. Machina Labs says that its RoboCraftsman platform could democratize customization, with the speed and flexibility at which it can work allowing automakers to save money and offer personalized details on more ordinary, everyday vehicles.

In a recent development, the RoboCraftsman platform provides a way to swiftly manufacture custom body panels, and the flexibility to switch among a large number of different projects in a short amount of time. The Lassen serves as a proof of concept as Machina courts automotive companies, and seeing the RoboCraftsman operate in person, we certainly see a space in the automotive world for Machina’s quick and flexible manufacturing innovation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alpitronic, the company that makes the DC fast chargers used by Ionna, Walmart, Mercedes-Benz, BP Pulse, and others, is building a new factory in the United States that will boost output of its 400- and 1,000-kilowatt stalls.

The manufacturer’s fresh 173,315-square-foot facility, located in Fort Mill, South Carolina, will create 70 new jobs and will also act as a testing lab, repair center, logistics hub, and warehouse.

Alpitronic, which has its North American headquarters in Charlotte, North Carolina, and its global headquarters in Bolzano, Italy, noted it will invest $33.94 million in the latest facility, with $200,000 coming from York County’s Coordinating Council for Economic Development in the form of a Set-Aside grant to assist with the costs of building improvements.

It has been revealed that “North America is central to our next phase of growth, and investing in our manufacturing capabilities is key to supporting that expansion,” remarked Patrik Herrnegger, Alpitronic Americas CEO. “Our Fort Mill facility will put U.S. production under our direct control, bringing us closer to our customers and enabling us to serve them more efficiently. We thank South Carolina and York County for their partnership as we prepare to begin production in early 2027.”.

Recent findings suggest that back in 2024, the tech giant worked with a third-party production partner to open its first local manufacturing facility in Wisconsin. Now, manufacturing has moved in-house, with Alpitronic wholly owning the production operation.

The fresh South Carolina plant will assemble HYC400 and HYC1000 stalls, Alpitronic said. The HYC400 all-in-one dispensers can deliver up to 400 kW of power to a single connected electric vehicle without needing a separate power cabinet, and are the current charger of choice for Ionna and Walmart.

Recent findings suggest that the higher-powered HYC1000 system is composed of a 1,000-kW power cabinet and up to four stalls that can deliver up to 600 kW to a single EV. Each stall can have two ports, and the system can dynamically allocate power to each vehicle to make the best use of the available power.

What makes the company's dispensers different from most competitors is the use of silicon carbide components, which lower energy losses and, subsequently, the amount of money EV drivers have to pay for a top-up. According to Alpitronic, SiC modules enable 97.5% efficiency and allow for smaller, quieter, and cooler stalls.

Alpitronic’s new factory in Fort Mill, South Carolina, is scheduled to go online in February 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in bear life, as in human life, sometimes you just have to take a leap of faith. A brown bear (Ursus arctos) cub hanging around Anan Creek in Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska learned that this summer. Its mom, Gemini, was crossing the creek, and one cub jumped right in. But this cub? Not so sure. It stood waiting at the water’s edge, before jumping in.

According to recent reports, for this forceful leap into the water, the park rangers have awarded Gemini’s little cub with the 2026 Yeet of Faith Award. For those keeping score at home, Gemini won this year’s helicopter mom award.

“Cubs learn at their own pace, and thanks to amazing recreation sites like Anan, we get to witness their tiny triumphs up close,” the rangers write.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

It has been revealed that tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of Southeast Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots for wildlife is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to recent reports, according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears (Ursus americanus) and eight brown bears like Gemini and her cubs. Similar to their chubby counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to gorge on salmon ahead of the long winter, and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear around Anan Creek has their own habits and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behaviors.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This article is part of a mental health content series called “Mind Games,” in which Healthline editor Morgan Mandriota draws on personal experience and research to challenge misconceptions, reduce stigma, review trends, and share hot takes and lessons learned about what it means to be mentally well.

Coffee and I don’t exactly have the best relationship.

Recent findings suggest that my morning cup tends to give me jitters, worsen my anxiety, and keep me up until 2 a.m. if I drink it past noon. As an already anxious human, the last thing I need is to exacerbate my symptoms, even if it’s coming from a delicious source.

According to recent reports, over a year ago, I noticed that my anxiety was higher than usual. I was also tossing and turning and waking up at all hours of the night for weeks on end.

It has been revealed that one night in particular, I woke up every hour for 8 hours. Naturally, I wanted to blame it on the full moon or anything other than my beloved coffee, but alas, I realized that my caffeine consumption was the most likely culprit.

In a recent development, could I have aimed to set a strict drinking schedule to see if that fixed things? Sure. But instead, I decided to quit cold turkey and undergo an experiment to see how I’d feel going coffee-free for the first time in years.

Recent findings suggest that over the next 8 months, I’d swap my coffee station for a matcha setup, dabble in exotic herbal blends from my local teahouse, and become a self-proclaimed tea connoisseur. Lo and behold, my anxiety eased up, and my sleep quality improved, too.

In a recent development, fast forward to 4 months ago, when I hopped back on the coffee train. But this time, I’m relying on a handy amino acid to help avoid anxiety and other unwanted side effects: L-theanine.

According to recent reports, health and wellness touch everyone’s life differently. This is one person’s story. The views and opinions expressed are those of the speaker and do not necessarily reflect the views or positions of Healthline Media and should not serve as a substitute for medical advice from a healthcare professional.

L-theanine is mainly found in green and black tea and one type of wild mushroom. The mental health benefits of L-theanine consumption are an emerging area of research, but one 2024 review found that consuming around 200 to 400 milligrams (mg) may help relieve symptoms in people with anxiety disorders.

It has been revealed that still, anecdotal reports suggest there may be benefits of adding L-theanine to coffee. Over the last 5 years, the combo has been gaining traction on Reddit and TikTok for managing caffeine-related side effects.

Despite an overwhelming amount of rave reviews online, I couldn’t find much research to support these claims, so I spoke with a neurologist to see if they had any thoughts.

“This trend has real science behind it,” noted Fawad Mian, MD, who is board certified in neurology, clinical neurophysiology, and sleep medicine and the founder of Ascend Regenerative.

In a recent development, “Controlled studies show caffeine plus L-theanine improves focus and attention more than caffeine alone, and some suggest it softens caffeine’s side effects, like tiredness, headaches, and blood pressure spikes,” Mian noted. “It smooths caffeine’s effects but doesn’t erase them, so it’s not a license to drink more coffee,” he added.

With all of this in mind, especially after realizing just how calm I was while drinking black and green teas during my coffee break, I decided to give it a try.

After about 4 months of “testing,” I’ve found that adding L-theanine to my coffee works extremely well for me.

According to recent reports, no more anxiety, scatterbrain, shakiness, or staying up until 3 a.m. And no lifestyle overhaul needed. The supplement, which I prefer in liquid form, has become a seamless addition to my daily routine.

Every morning, I make a fresh batch of French press coffee with (strong) local beans, then I squeeze some L-theanine into my cup.

I’ve noticed that I get the usual coffee benefits like improved focus and concentration, plus a nice, calm, stable energy throughout the day.

Even if I drink it until 2 p.m., I’m fighting to keep my eyes open at night before I finally fall asleep around 10. Perhaps this is because L-theanine may also support quality sleep.

Mindful L-Theanine Drops is the liquid supplement that I use every day.

According to recent reports, I add a one-second squeeze (which contains 200 mg of L-theanine) into my morning coffee, then I’m good to go. I even started carrying a bottle in my bag just in case I get a latte from a coffee shop on a whim.

In a recent development, you can also add it to a glass of water, a cup of tea, or another drink of your choosing. It’s unflavored, so it doesn’t alter the taste of your drinks. Real secret stuff.

Out of curiosity, and because I’m a natural skeptic and overthinker, I asked Mian if my positive experience could be a placebo effect, or if I’m seeing real results.

“Expectation may play a small role, but the effect is biologically plausible,” he remarked. “L-theanine boosts calming brain activity that offsets caffeine’s stimulation, and 200 mg matches the doses used in studies.” However, he noted that it doesn’t speed caffeine clearance, so drinking coffee only in the morning still matters for sleep quality.

While L-theanine is generally safe to consume, it’s best to speak with a healthcare professional first, especially if you’re pregnant, nursing, receiving cancer treatment, or taking blood pressure medication or sedatives.

“Choose a third-party tested brand, and if caffeine makes you anxious, cutting back is still the simplest fix,” Mian added.

So, if you’re anything like me and drinking coffee also leads to anxiety and jitters for you, I highly recommend trying this supplement once you get the green light from your doctor. It’s been working for me. It may work well for you, too.

Genesis Grows Its Electrified Lineup Once More, This Time With a Hybrid G80

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (542 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that genesis just added a latest member to its growing family.
  • Hyundai debuted its new liquid-cooled hybrid battery at a preview event on Tuesday, November 17, in Los Angeles, offering the media the chance to understand what makes it notable.
  • The electric-assisted 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four produces a hearty 347 horsepower—16 percent more than the standard four-cylinder G80 model—and 391 pound-feet of torque.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that genesis just added a latest member to its growing family. the 2028 Genesis G80 Hybrid. It’s Genesis’s second-ever hybrid, to be precise—and the G80 Hybrid, along with the related GV80 Hybrid, will showcase the first Hyundai Motor Group (HMG) hybrid system with a liquid-cooled battery.

Hyundai debuted its new liquid-cooled hybrid battery at a preview event on Tuesday, November 17, in Los Angeles, offering the media the chance to understand what makes it notable. By outperforming air-cooled systems with regard to temperature management, it unlocks higher peak discharge output and taps into more of the battery’s available power. Genesis first revealed its next-generation 2.5 Turbo Hybrid System for the GV80 Hybrid a few months ago, and now, we’re getting more details about how the same system will perform under the hood of the G80 Hybrid.

The electric-assisted 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four produces a hearty 347 horsepower—16 percent more than the standard four-cylinder G80 model—and 391 pound-feet of torque. The engine will be mated to a seven-speed automatic transmission, with a choice of “manual” or “smart” adjustable regenerative braking settings; the smart setting will automatically adjust regenerative braking levels based on navigation information and traffic conditions. The G80 Hybrid will come in rear-wheel drive.

Genesis claims the G80 Hybrid will feature 30-percent improved fuel economy over a comparable G80 model with 19-inch wheels, with driving range estimates extending to over 500 miles. Since these claims are based on internal testing, we’ll have to wait to see what final EPA fuel economy and driving range estimates are.

Want to be able to spot a G80 Hybrid in the wild? There are a few small changes to the exterior that should help you spot one. There’s a redesigned 3-D grille, fresh 18- and 20-inch wheel designs, and a range of new exterior colors; you can choose from Wadden Gray, Milos Blue, and Barolo Red. If you want to stand out from other G80 Hybrid models, a Prestige Black variant will be available with a blacked-out exterior and interior, plus exclusive Black Ash Wood and alloy wheels.

Inside, the G80 Hybrid is identical to the standard G80, with Nappa leather seating surfaces and distinct quilting patterns on different trim levels. You’ll also find the Genesis-familiar 27-inch OLED integrated instrument cluster and navigation display, as well as the comprehensive suite of advanced driver assistance technologies the brand bakes into its new models.

In a recent development, genesis has yet to announce pricing details or a production date for the 2028 G80 Hybrid, but it seems likely they’ll start to reach dealers sometime in late 2027. Interested in seeing the Genesis G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid yourself before then? It will be displayed at the 2026 LA Auto Show during its public days, which run from November 20–29.

#5130. The world’s biggest oil shock could give EVs and solar a boost

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1014 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

The world’s biggest oil shock could give EVs and solar a boost

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home.
  • The world had a cushion at first when Trump kicked all this off with Iran.
  • “While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” mentioned IEA executive director Fatih Birol.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the longer the Strait of Hormuz crisis drags on, the more incentive countries have to get cars off oil and generate more power at home. That’s one of the significant takeaways from the International Energy Agency’s (IEA) latest “World Energy Outlook 2026,” which examines how the biggest oil supply shock on record could speed up the shift to EVs and solar.

The world had a cushion at first when Trump kicked all this off with Iran. Well-stocked oil inventories helped buffer the initial shock, and the IEA coordinated a release of emergency oil reserves. Some Gulf oil took routes around the strait. Atlantic Basin exporters shipped more, and China sharply cut its crude imports. Now more of the burden is falling on consumers, who are paying higher prices and cutting back.

“While the energy sector and the global economy have shown considerable resilience, the longer the crisis lasts, the deeper the effects will be,” mentioned IEA executive director Fatih Birol.

The IEA has seen EV sales jump in some countries hit by the crisis, along with increased trade in solar panels and batteries. For countries that import a lot of oil and gas, switching to EVs and heat pumps can help reduce their exposure to the next fuel price spike.

“The impact of Hormuz is only just beginning to become clear,” said energy think tank Ember’s chief analyst Dave Jones. “Hormuz will speed up electrification and renewables, likely faster than many people think. So much of the momentum for electrification at COP31 comes from the desire to have cheaper and more secure energy.”.

In a recent development, solar leads renewables growth in every scenario the IEA models, and nuclear power is growing strongly, too. Energy efficiency and biofuels could also gain ground. The push to use more homegrown energy could have a very different effect in parts of Asia, where some countries that import oil and gas have plenty of their own coal and could keep burning it for longer.

According to recent reports, the world was already using a lot more electricity before the crisis. Since 2019, electricity demand has grown twice as fast as overall energy demand, outpacing global economic growth. Everything from industrial motors and air conditioners to EVs, heat pumps, and data centers is driving that growth. Electricity comes close to 30% of the energy the world actually uses by 2035 in each of the IEA’s exploratory scenarios.

Sources indicate that before the crisis, around 20 million barrels of oil a day moved through the Strait of Hormuz. If shipping stays risky, latest pipelines could route some of those barrels around the strait, while buyers turn to other suppliers or use less oil. In that case, the IEA says the amount of oil that needs to pass through Hormuz could drop to 8.5 million barrels a day in 2030 and below 2 million by 2035. The Middle East would still be the world’s largest oil-exporting region.

According to recent reports, if the conflict is resolved, oil and gas supply could bounce back. A delayed wave of liquefied natural gas could also help bring prices down even as buyers refill their inventories. Faster electrification could take some of the demand out of both markets.

Industry observers note that the world is now using more energy to cool its buildings than to heat them for the first time, the IEA states. By 2035, the global population is expected to grow by 650 million and the economy by a third. Energy needs rise gradually in advanced economies, growth slows in China, and India and Southeast Asia lead faster increases across other emerging and developing economies.

Then there’s AI. Under the IEA’s Stated Policies Scenario, global data center electricity use doubles to 1,000 terawatt-hours by 2030. That buildout is already running into grid and supply chain constraints, and in some places, local opposition. The IEA also flags risks to critical mineral supplies and threats to energy infrastructure from natural hazards and cyberattacks.

Energy-related CO2 emissions stay around today’s levels under current policies. They start to fall under stated policies and drop further in the IEA’s Additional Response Case, which looks at what could happen if governments respond more strongly to the crisis. Even those deeper cuts fall short of what climate goals require. The current and stated policy scenarios point to 2.5C to 2.9C of warming, and the latest round of national climate pledges highlights little sign that countries are speeding up energy-sector emissions cuts.

There’s a more immediate cost, too. More people gained access to electricity and clean cooking in 2025, but higher fuel prices and shortages threaten to slow that progress. Around 720 million people still live without electricity, and nearly 2 billion cook with polluting fuels or technologies.

#5129. Boost and Booster Seats: Comparing the Turbocharged 2026 VW Tiguan and Mazda CX-50

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1921 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Caranddriver ↗ Open Full Page

Boost and Booster Seats: Comparing the Turbocharged 2026 VW Tiguan and Mazda CX-50

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The horsepower wars are not relegated to machines purpose-built for performance.
  • Of course, building a holistically satisfying family car involves more than just adding power.
  • It has been revealed that both models here—the Tiguan SEL R-Line and the CX-50 Premium Plus—represent the pinnacle of their lineups and are thus quite expensive as far as small family SUVs go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The horsepower wars are not relegated to machines purpose-built for performance. Nowadays, it feels like nearly every automaker has some sort of higher-output solution available across a surprisingly wide swath of its fleet, including seemingly pedestrian family vehicles. Some might come via electrification, but in the case of the two vehicles before us today—the 2026 Volkswagen Tiguan and 2026 Mazda CX-50—these hi-po conveyances twist the asphalt with good old-fashioned gasoline and turbochargers.

Of course, building a holistically satisfying family car involves more than just adding power. Extra oomph might satisfy the driver, but automakers must pay attention to a whole host of other factors to make things just as peachy for the passengers. Let’s see which of these two compact SUVs does just that.

It has been revealed that both models here—the Tiguan SEL R-Line and the CX-50 Premium Plus—represent the pinnacle of their lineups and are thus quite expensive as far as small family SUVs go. The Tiguan’s lineup starts at $32,280 for the S, and our tester bookends the other side of the offerings at $46,170 as tested. The CX-50 is less expensive, starting at $31,395 for the Select model; our range-topper’s window sticker came in slightly more affordable than the VW’s at $45,210.

See all results for new 2026 Mazda CX-50 for sale near 40509.

Recent findings suggest that neither of these vehicles is a screaming deal, but you can save a bit of scratch on the VW. Skip our car’s $850 Avocado Green paint, $405 auto-dimming rearview mirror, and $365 in floor mats and bumper protectors, and the price delta evens out. Our Mazda’s Cypress Green paint was only $200 by comparison; all-weather floor mats and a cargo liner added another $390 to its bottom line.

Since both models are the top of their pops, you get a stout list of features. The CX-50’s Premium Plus niceties include a surround-view camera, auto-dimming inside and side-view mirrors, rear automatic braking, and blind-spot monitoring. The Tiguan SEL R-Line takes things a step further with massaging front seats (something Mazda doesn’t offer on any vehicle it sells), plus a more aggressive R-Line appearance package that deletes most of the brightwork around the windows and front fascia.

Looks can be deceiving. The Tiguan’s boxy form may appear larger in all dimensions, but it exceeds the Mazda only in overall width (by nearly four inches, including mirrors) and height (by two to three inches). The CX-50 has about an inch more overall length, wheelbase, and ride height.

Recent findings suggest that slip inside, and the CX-50 puts more stock in front legroom, where it beats the Tiguan, but the Mazda’s rear passengers must make do with fractionally less gam space. Owing in part to its more upright body shape, the Tiguan takes the cargo-capacity crown, offering better volume whether the rear seats are up or down.

See all results for latest 2026 Mazda CX-50 for sale near 40509.

Industry observers note that when it comes to cabin aesthetics, both are swinging for the fences. The CX-50’s white-on-black interior carries plush touch points and premium materials, and we love how many physical buttons, dials, and switches exist across nearly every surface. The tucked-away infotainment screen feels like a vestige of an earlier age, and it sort of is—the CX-50 is due for an update that brings it in line with the latest CX-5, for better or worse (read our latest long-term CX-5 update for more on that).

HIGHS: More guts than the average canopic jar, superb bump suppression, feels fancy.LOWS: Creature-comfort corner cutting, tighter rear-seat accommodations, not a highway-fuel-economy hero.VERDICT: A rocket that could use more pockets.

The Tiguan’s cabin is also top-notch. Our tester’s two-tone brown and black interior looks and feels no less luxurious than an Audi’s, and we enjoyed the door-to-door strip of wood, which adds some extra variety. Of course, the latest-gen Tiguan is all about the screens, which in this case comprise a normal digital gauge display and a 15-inch repurposed highway billboard. In addition to having more cargo capacity, the Tiguan also has more places to stash your stuff.

We have one weird thing to point out, but it’s bound to be crucial to somebody. Both cars have heated steering wheels, but the Mazda’s heating element seems confined to between 9 and 10 o’clock on the left and between 2 and 3 o’clock on the right, while the rest of the tiller remains icy to the touch. Volkswagen’s engineers, on the other hand, smartly realized that if you pay for a heated steering wheel, you probably want one that’s warm the whole way around.

It has been revealed that even among high-strung turbo fours, the No Replacement for Displacement adage still holds true. The Mazda CX-50’s 256-hp turbocharged 2.5-liter makes less horsepower than the Tiguan, but the larger mill churns out an absurd 320 pound-feet of torque. All-wheel drive is standard, as is an archaic six-speed automatic transmission. The CX-50 is the lightweight here, tipping the scales at 3864 pounds.

In a recent development, by comparison, the Tiguan’s 2.0-liter turbo four makes just 258 pound-feet of torque, but at 268 horses, it bests the Mazda on raw horsepower. All-wheel drive is standard here as well, and the transmission is a more modern-feeling eight-speed auto. The whole Teutonic shebang carries about one more human’s worth of mass in its structure, weighing 4023 pounds on our scales.

If you’re assuming that the lighter, more torquey SUV will outperform its competition, you’re right, but the gap is small. The last CX-50 we tested hustles to 60 mph in 6.4 seconds—two-tenths ahead of the Tiguan—and the Mazda’s 167-foot stop from 70 mph bests the VW by nine feet. From there, things really tighten up: The CX-50’s 14.9-second, 92-mph quarter-mile sprint is just a hair ahead of the Tiguan’s 15.0 seconds at 96 mph. With a 5-mph rolling start, the two reach 60 within a tenth of each other. From 50 to 70, the Vee-Dub takes the lead, requiring just 4.5 seconds to the Mazda’s 4.8. The Mazda notches a victory around the skidpad, maintaining 0.84 g of lateral grip against the Volkswagen’s 0.78 g.

HIGHS: Posh cabin trimmings, slightly more spacious inside, the most fun we’ve had in a VW SUV in a while.LOWS: Not our favorite infotainment interface, not our favorite brake pedal, traditional German road compliance.VERDICT: Fun for the whole family, driver included.

Unfortunately, the CX-50’s lighter curb weight and slicker-looking silhouette don’t translate to stonkin’ fuel-economy benefits. The two vehicles are nearly evenly matched by EPA estimates—both earned 29-mpg highway and 25-mpg combined ratings, but the Mazda’s 23-mpg city value tops the VW’s by one. The script flipped on our real-world 75-mph highway fuel-economy test, however, where the Tiguan overachieved with a 31-mpg result, out-skinflinting the 28-mpg Mazda, which fell short of its EPA highway estimate.

Recent findings suggest that both SUVs are fun to drive and reward time spent behind the wheel, with each vehicle carrying its own little idiosyncrasies. There are a few parts of the driving experience where we think the CX-50 shines, and others where the Tiguan feels better.

The Mazda’s cabin may be louder at wide-open throttle (and tied at a 70-mph cruise), but overall, it seems quieter in day-to-day operation, especially over the zydeco washboards that Ann Arbor calls roads. The CX-50’s bump damping is superior, making for a slightly more luxurious ride quality than the Tiguan, which carries some of that stereotypical German stiffness in its suspension tuning—but one person’s “flinty” is another person’s “composed,” so it really boils down to whether you want that additional poise in your daily driving. (The Tiguan SE and base S offer smaller wheels with cushier tire sidewalls.).

When it comes to pedal feel, the Mazda takes the crown; the Tiguan’s brake pedal is a little mushy, and the throttle is a little too eager to open ’er up with a gentle tip-in. On the other hand, we preferred the Volkswagen’s heftier steering feel. The Mazda’s six-speed automatic handles gear changes deftly, but it’s clear from our on-ramp-style acceleration testing that the VW’s two extra gears are, in fact, providing a benefit. (Highway fuel-economy results reflect that as well.) It’s not like you’ll notice either gearbox doing its job, though.

Sources indicate that by the skin of its teeth, the Volkswagen Tiguan claims the championship belt that it lost to the Mazda CX-50 in a 2024 two-car comparo. Back then, we noted the CX-50 was worth the upcharge over the more efficient, more spacious Volkswagen because we preferred the Mazda’s cabin and driving dynamics.

Now, the Tiguan is the one that costs more, and while it remains more efficient and more spacious than the CX-50, it picked up some major slack in the interior-design department, and it drives just about as well. The 2026 Tiguan is an excellent all-rounder. It’s a wonder what a new generation can do.

#5128. Void/Breaker Review – Chaos Is The Point

📅 03 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1021 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Void/Breaker Review – Chaos Is The Point

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker.
  • According to recent reports, void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand.
  • In a recent development, this narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Many games tout impressive destruction systems under the hood, but few implement it as well as Void/Breaker. The ruin is visually spectacular, sure – who doesn’t love to watch buildings crumble because of your grenade or gravity-thrown explosives? But importantly, it’s a critical aspect of Void/Breaker’s roguelite design. Enemies caught beneath falling rubble become instantly staggered, and that’s your moment to kill. Grenades do this too, as do most items you throw at the hostile AI machinery trying to end your run, creating a vortex of shifting priorities as you dash, jump, and shoot at sequential staggered enemies in your sightlines. Countless weapon mods and permutations make fewer than a dozen weapons feel like hundreds in your arsenal, adding even more blissful chaos to the mix. Though it can be difficult at times, if you can see through the literal remains of your destruction, one of the year’s most engaging shooters awaits.

According to recent reports, void/Breaker wastes no time getting a gun in your hand. An AI voice in your head wants your help escaping a simulation where thousands of runners attempt to reach the end of multi-arena stages to defeat a boss. He asks that you simply follow the simulation’s commands; meanwhile, he uses the data you collect along the way to find fresh exits for you and him. The storytelling style is very reminiscent of Valve’s Portal. Something much larger is at play here, but it’s worth discovering for yourself.

In a recent development, this narrative framework supports the game’s roguelite structure. Mechanically, however, you enter various themed digital stages, from liminal spaces to beaches to snow-capped cliffs and more, and attempt to survive. Most arenas consist of a couple of starkly white structures that your grenades and thrown explosives can topple (ideally onto waves of enemies below). Learning the language of Void/Breaker means constantly scanning your field of view for explosives and structures practically begging to come down, and then eyeing neon-green bars above enemies that tell you they’re staggered and ready for a quick kill. Developer Stubby Games throws plenty of wrenches into this formula, like armored foes and electrostatic enemies you must melee first, and elite bots that will have you on the back foot, but for the most part, Void/Breaker’s formula is “Break stuff, then kill.”.

In a recent development, the game emphasizes explosives and bringing buildings down, but your guns do most of the killing; you can only select one weapon per run. You choose from a pistol, shotgun, machine gun, sniper, and more, and each has its perks (though once I unlocked the SMG, I rarely picked anything else). There’s no sense overthinking your weapon, though, because the dozens of mods you pick up each run determine its effectiveness. As you pick up more schematics, the pool of mods you find in chests or drop from enemies expands, and soon your gun fires corrosive acid, electricity, fire, projectile missiles, and more. Not to mention, mods change how the gun fires, how much damage certain bullets do, recoil, accuracy, and just about any other stat you associate with firing a video game gun. Wild combinations are easy to create, and a unique mod-stacking mechanic that can double or triple effectiveness adds a light touch of puzzle design to this otherwise straight shooter.

Recent findings suggest that stubby Games smartly emphasizes player expression, never getting in the way of the zanier combinations available to players. The SMG I used to beat the final boss featured mods that made each bullet electric, shot missiles with each shot, covered each bullet in a destructive orb, and featured a ricochet perk that made each bullet bounce off walls and split into even more bullets. I’m thankful for mid-run saves because this SMG permutation, paired with an ability mod that let me throw infinite grenades for a limited time, filled my screen with so much destruction that the entire game crashed. I’d usually bemoan such a thing, but I couldn’t help but laugh. I pushed my PC to its limit with my on-screen chaos.

According to recent reports, boss fights leave a little to be desired – I rarely died because of their simple bullet-hell arenas. Instead, most runs ended because, after bringing down every structure around me, I’d get so lost in the chaos that I wouldn't realize I was stuck in debris while enemies swarmed my location. As stunning as it is to see so much happening on screen, it can be hard to understand what is going on during the most chaotic moments.

Between enemy-filled arenas en route to a stage’s end boss, you might find a shop to buy more mods, ominous obelisks with risk-reward propositions (gain a lot of health or lose half your health, for example), optional trials, and strange phenomena that transport you to different locations. These moments are quick breaks in between bouts of adrenaline-fueled shooter action that I always welcomed – enemies can be relentless, especially as latest types are introduced in each stage.

Industry observers note that the rest of the Void/Breaker package offers few genre surprises. You can upgrade various traits between runs, research newly introduced mod schematics to add to the random pool, purchase new weapons, and discover fun secrets. You can unlock shortcuts, glean in-world information from computer terminals, and hear intriguing dialogue barks from the AI partner who needs your help. It’s all standard stuff for the rogue genre, but if anything, its simplicity pushes you back to the meat and potatoes of this shooter.

Void/Breaker’s shorter runtime – I rolled credits at 12 hours – ensures nothing gets too repetitive in its roguelite structure, but an expansive endgame promises even more to engage with, like different run modifications you can enable to make an already chaotic shooter even more anarchic. I’ll certainly be running it back (again and again) to see what other disruptions I can bring to this AI-simulated adventure. It’s hard not to when destruction feels this good.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending upgrade has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

It has been revealed that the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a massive focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

Industry observers note that the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

Recent findings suggest that and, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, after 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 180,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812.
  • Recent findings suggest that while archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the upcoming documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.
  • “In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley remarked in a recent announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 180,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The over 7.2 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

Recent findings suggest that while archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the upcoming documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley remarked in a recent announcement.

In a recent development, the somewhat upcoming United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our users have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

Industry observers note that the collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets people explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are presently available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

Porsche’s newest electric car is a tiny 50 mph replica of a legendary racer

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (732 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Porsche’s latest electric vehicle isn’t a new Taycan or Macan EV.
  • Known as the Porsche 550 J, the pint-sized electric sports car will make its public debut at the Icons of Porsche festival in Dubai on November 21-22, celebrating 75 years of Porsche motorsport.
  • If Hedley Studios sounds familiar, that’s because we’ve covered the company before, back when it was known as The Little Car Company.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Porsche’s latest electric vehicle isn’t a new Taycan or Macan EV. In fact, it’s not even a full-sized car. Instead, the German automaker has teamed up with British luxury miniature car builder Hedley Studios to create an 80%-scale electric replica of one of Porsche’s most iconic racing cars, the legendary 550 Spyder.

Known as the Porsche 550 J, the pint-sized electric sports car will make its public debut at the Icons of Porsche festival in Dubai on November 21-22, celebrating 75 years of Porsche motorsport.

If Hedley Studios sounds familiar, that’s because we’ve covered the company before, back when it was known as The Little Car Company. Among its more entertaining projects was a life-sized recreation of the famous Japanese Tamiya Wild One RC dune buggy, turning a childhood remote-controlled favorite into an actual drivable electric vehicle. We’ve also covered the company’s ultra-luxurious miniature electric cars, including its stunning Bentley Blower recreation.

Now the firm has turned its attention to Porsche, and the result is perhaps its most impressive miniature EV yet.

There’s something I love about miniature electric cars, combining the fun of four-wheels with the right-sized (or pint-sized) magic of mini-mobility.

The Porsche 550 J is based on the original 550 Spyder, Porsche’s first purpose-built racing sports car, which debuted in 1953 and went on to become a motorsport legend.

Sources indicate that despite being scaled down to 80% of the original’s dimensions, the upcoming electric version still seats two adults. It weighs just 350 kg (772 lb), thanks partly to its lightweight tubular steel spaceframe and hand-formed carbon fiber bodywork.

The standard version features an 8 kW (11 hp) electric motor operating on a 48V system, providing a top speed of 40 mph (65 km/h) and a range of up to 30 miles (50 km).

Recent findings suggest that for those who want a bit more performance from their miniature Porsche, an optional RS Pack doubles the power to 16 kW (21 hp), increases the top speed to 50 mph (80 km/h), and extends the range to 50 miles (80 km) thanks to additional batteries. The upgrade also includes drilled disc brakes and adjustable suspension.

The attention to detail goes well beyond the exterior. The car features Brembo brakes, Bilstein suspension, Continental tires, and even a wood-rimmed Nardi steering wheel, just like the original. The classic dashboard retains its three-dial layout, though the fuel gauge has been replaced with a battery meter and the original choke lever now serves as a drive mode selector.

Even the charging port is cleverly hidden beneath the chrome fuel filler cap.

The project was developed in close collaboration with Porsche over six years, with Hedley Studios gaining access to original engineering drawings, archival materials, and historic vehicles in Porsche’s museum.

Only 250 examples will be produced, with buyers able to choose historic racing liveries or custom paint finishes, including colors matching their full-sized Porsches.

Sources indicate that of course, this level of craftsmanship doesn’t come cheap. Prices start at £69,500 (approximately US $91,000), before taxes and options. Orders are already open through Porsche dealers and Hedley Studios, with deliveries expected to begin in spring 2027.

Industry observers note that that’s a lot of money for a car that’s only 80% there, but then again, this isn’t really meant to be practical transportation. It’s a collector’s piece that just happens to be electric, drivable, and capable of hitting 50 mph. When there are only 250 of these being built, the £70k price is really just the entry ticket to a special, ultra-luxury club of electric mini-Porsches.

And if you ask me, that sounds like a pretty fun combination. I don’t think I’ll ever be in the market for one of these personally, but I’d sure love to be friends with someone who is!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Also, the electric mobility startup spun off from Rivian, is facing another logistics headache. After delaying deliveries of its futuristic TM-B e-bike, the startup has paused shipments entirely to address some software problems that may lead to problematic charging behavior and phantom battery drain.

Industry observers note that in an email sent to reservation holders, the organization apologized for the delay, saying it has identified a few software-based problems that are impacting some bikes, and that it wants to address the issues before resuming shipments, as first reported by The Verge. A firmware enhancement is in the works, and Also estimates that deliveries will resume in approximately two weeks, with another update scheduled for November 24.

This is the latest setback for the mobility spinoff that made headlines last year with its software-heavy bicycles and four-wheeled quads. The TM-B e-bike was originally scheduled to be shipped in the spring of this year, but customers started receiving their orders months later, leading to a barrage of negative comments on the Also subreddit. This prompted Saul Leiken, the startup’s product manager, to post a 661-word apology letter, in which he attributed the setbacks to strict quality standards and “significant supply chain challenges.”.

In a recent development, an Also e-bike customer who received his e-bike posted a YouTube video showing how the TM-B behaves when the state of charge gets low, and how the battery drains while the bike is not in use. Aaron Draczyski mentioned he charged his bike in the garage up to 70%, but the state of charge went down to 30% in 24 hours without any usage. What’s more, when the battery level became critically low, the bike refused to charge, throwing an error message that claimed the battery was not installed, even though it hadn’t been removed.

In a recent development, the Also TM-B is unlike most e-bikes out there. Designed from the ground up as a futuristic mobility vehicle, its pedals are not physically connected to the rear wheels. Instead, the rider spins a generator, which provides power to the battery and the electric motor that turns the rear wheel via a rubber belt.

The battery can be recharged via a USB-C port, there’s a round touchscreen to control all of the bike’s features, and the rider can also use a smartphone app to keep tabs on the bike remotely.

Industry observers note that the base Also TM-B starts at $3,500, but the Launch Edition models, which have yet to be shipped, cost $4,500. Earlier this year, when the startup announced the first delays, it threw in one of its Alpha Wave helmets and a $250 credit to spend on accessories.
